name: Vale
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: No grammar or phonology of Vale (CAR) located online

sources.citation: Moéhama, Elisée. 2021. Rapport d'enquête sociolinguistique: Première évaluation parmi les Vale. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-025, 28 pp. SIL International (Glottolog ref 588593)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey only; the one mention of 'accents' (§3.1.1) refers to regional accent differences between the Tane and Bouna sub-groups, not word stress.

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2006. Présentation des langues Sara-Bongo-Baguirmiennes (comparative overview of SBB; already on file under luto1241)
sources.note: Grep of the text layer: no occurrence of 'accent'/'stress'/'intensité' in a stress sense; Vale is mentioned only in the classification. Not a Vale description.

sources.citation: Olson, Kenneth S. 2024. A preliminary phonology of Vale. In Yaqian Huang, Nina Hagen Kaldhol, Jun Jie Lim, Sharon Rose & Anthony Struthers-Young (eds.), ACAL in SoCAL: Selected papers from the 53rd Annual Conference on African Linguistics, 455–474. Berlin: Language Science Press. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.11210474
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: Harvard print copy (Scan & Deliver or loan); the journal or volume is held, not the item itself: WID Offsite Storage PL8002.C65 2022
sources.note: Nothing: the words 'stress' and 'accent' do not occur in the chapter. It describes a two-level tone system (H, L), five underlying melodies L/H/LH/HL/HLH, TBU = mora (pp. 462–466); no statement on word stress or prominence.

sources.citation: Yanguende, Simplice. 2011. Phonologie et morphologie des nominaux du vale de Ndélé en Centrafrique. Mémoire de Master 2, Institut de Linguistique Appliquée, Université de Bangui. 163 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives 93213)
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent; ch. IV 'Tonématique' (p. 61 ff.) states 'Le vâlé, à l'instar des langues africaines, est une langue à ton' and inventories 3 level tones (H, M, B) + 2 contour tones. Identity doubtful: Olson 2024: 469–470 argues this 'Vale de Ndélé' is probably Luto (Ndoka or Wad) rather than Vale.

sources.citation: Bruel, Georges. 1905. Le cercle du Moyen-Logone. Paris: Comité de l'Afrique française (Vale number list, 'Télé de Guélo', p. 100); Gaudefroy-Demombynes, Maurice. 1906. Documents sur les langues de l'Oubangui-Chari (Vale numbers and vocabulary, p. 60)
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only pre-2011 Vale data (per Olson 2024: 456); wordlists only, very unlikely to state stress, but they are the remaining primary records on Glottolog's list.

sources.citation: Olson, Kenneth S. (in progress) — fuller phonology / lexicon of Vale by the same SIL/ACATBA team (Olson 2024 §6–§7 lists tone in the TAM system and word patterns as next steps); no such publication located as of 2026-09-17
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only researcher with Vale data; any follow-up would be the first place a stress/prominence remark on Vale could appear. Nothing found to fetch; listed so the gap is tracked.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1/5.3 languoid vale1250 reference list (1 descriptive reference: Olson 2024, hhtype phonology) and Glottolog hh.bib records for [vae]: Bruel 1905 (overview/ethnographic, 'Télé de Guélo'), Gaudefroy-Demombynes 1906 (overview/wordlist), Moéhama 2021 (socling), Olson 2024 (phonology, 'Dogu Saki = Vale')
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: Bibliographic records only; the two colonial-era sources are number lists / short vocabularies (per Olson 2024: 456) and would not carry a stress statement.
